subject: Mathematics
title: Ravi and Priya's Candy Shop Adventure
hook: Can Ravi count all the candies before they melt?

slides.title: The Candy Shop Opens
slides.storyContext: Ravi visits Priya's family candy shop. Priya says, 'We got 100 candies today! Can you count them?'

points.label: Story start
points.text: Ravi and Priya stand in a bright candy shop with jars and jars of sweets.

slides.inSimpleWords: Ravi and Priya want to count 100 candies.

image.alt: The Candy Shop Opens — Numbers up to 100

slides.title: Counting by Ones
slides.storyContext: Ravi starts: 1, 2, 3... Priya counts along. They count to 10 and clap!
slides.inSimpleWords: Count by saying each number: one, two, three...

image.alt: Counting by Ones — Numbers up to 100

slides.title: Groups of 10
slides.storyContext: Priya puts 10 candies in each small bag. 'Look!' she says. 'One bag of 10, two bags of 10, three bags of 10!'

example.problem: If I have 3 bags with 10 candies each, how many candies?

slides.inSimpleWords: Groups of 10 help us count faster.

slides.title: Tens and Ones
slides.storyContext: Ravi sees 2 full bags (20) and 5 extra candies. 'That's twenty and five!' he says happily.
slides.inSimpleWords: Numbers have tens and ones parts.

image.alt: Tens and Ones — Numbers up to 100

slides.title: More Numbers
slides.storyContext: Priya counts aloud: 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30. Ravi joins: 31, 32... They keep going!
slides.inSimpleWords: After 9 ones, we get a new ten.

slides.title: How Many Candies?
slides.storyContext: Ravi has counted 50 candies. Priya says, 'There are 48 more left! Can you count them all?'
slides.inSimpleWords: We can reach 100 by counting higher!

image.alt: How Many Candies? — Numbers up to 100

slides.title: Reaching 100
slides.storyContext: Finally! 90, 91, 92... 98, 99, 100! All the candies are counted. Priya and Ravi high-five!
slides.inSimpleWords: 100 is the biggest number we learn.

slides.title: Numbers Before 100
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks, 'What numbers come before 100?' Priya answers: 95, 96, 97, 98, 99, 100!

example.solution: We go lower by one each time.

slides.inSimpleWords: Count up or down; both are fun!

slides.title: Ravi's Question
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks, 'If we have 45 candies in the window, how many more to make 100?'
slides.inSimpleWords: Subtraction helps us find how many more.

slides.title: Real-World Numbers
slides.storyContext: Priya shows Ravi price tags: ₹25, ₹50, ₹75. 'These numbers are in our shop every day!'

example.problem: A sweet costs ₹35. How many sweets for ₹100?
example.solution: About 2 or 3 sweets, depending on the kind.

slides.inSimpleWords: Numbers help us buy and sell things.

slides.title: Candy Shop Lesson
slides.storyContext: Ravi and Priya sit down to rest. They counted to 100 and learned that numbers help us understand the world.

points.label: What we learned
points.text: 1. Count by ones. 2. Count by tens. 3. Numbers up to 100 have tens and ones. 4. Numbers help in shops and homes.

slides.inSimpleWords: Numbers from 1 to 100 are our friends!

image.alt: Candy Shop Lesson — Numbers up to 100

subject: Mathematics
title: Priya's Magic Number Cards
hook: How do cards show us that 23 and 32 are different?

slides.title: A Box of Magic Cards
slides.storyContext: Priya pulls out two piles of cards: one with pictures of 10-pencils and one with pictures of single pencils. 'Ravi, let's build numbers!' she says.

points.label: Card piles
points.text: Tens cards and ones cards are like two different treasures.

slides.inSimpleWords: Place value cards help us see tens and ones.

image.alt: A Box of Magic Cards — Place Value

slides.title: Tens Place
slides.storyContext: Priya takes 3 tens-cards. 'Each card shows 10 pencils bundled together. So 3 tens-cards = 30 pencils!'
slides.inSimpleWords: The left number tells us how many tens.

slides.title: Ones Place
slides.storyContext: Ravi takes 5 ones-cards. 'These show 5 single pencils. Just 5!'
slides.inSimpleWords: The right number tells us how many ones.

slides.title: Building 35
slides.storyContext: Priya arranges 3 tens-cards (left side) and 5 ones-cards (right side). 'Together they make 35!'

example.problem: Show the number 35 with tens and ones cards.

slides.inSimpleWords: 3 tens + 5 ones = 35.

slides.title: The Swap Game
slides.storyContext: Priya swaps the position. Now 5 tens-cards are on the left and 3 ones-cards on the right. 'What number now, Ravi?'
slides.inSimpleWords: Swapping tens and ones changes the number!

slides.title: Place Value in 23
slides.storyContext: Ravi builds 23. 'I put 2 tens-cards and 3 ones-cards,' he says proudly.
slides.inSimpleWords: 2 in tens, 3 in ones = 23.

slides.title: Comparing Numbers
slides.storyContext: Priya shows two numbers: 45 (4 tens, 5 ones) and 54 (5 tens, 4 ones). 'Which is bigger, Ravi?'

example.solution: 54 is bigger because it has 5 tens (50), while 45 has only 4 tens (40).

slides.inSimpleWords: More tens means a bigger number!

slides.title: Ravi's Question
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks, 'In the number 67, which digit is in the tens place?' Priya smiles and points to the 6.

points.label: Tens digit
points.text: 6 is in the tens place. 7 is in the ones place.

slides.inSimpleWords: Name the tens and ones in any number!

slides.title: Real-Life Place Value
slides.storyContext: They see a price tag: ₹42. Priya says, 'That's 4 tens rupees and 2 ones rupees!'

example.problem: What is the place value of 4 in ₹42?
example.solution: 4 is in the tens place, so it means 4 × 10 = 40 rupees.

slides.inSimpleWords: Money uses place value too!

slides.title: Writing Place Value
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches Ravi to write: 30 + 7 = 37. 'The 3 is worth 30 because it's in the tens place!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Split numbers into tens and ones!

slides.title: Magic Card Magic
slides.storyContext: Ravi and Priya put the cards away. 'Now I know every digit has a job!' says Ravi. 'Tens on the left, ones on the right!'

points.label: Learning
points.text: 1. Every digit has a place. 2. Tens place is on the left. 3. Ones place is on the right. 4. Position changes the number's value.

slides.inSimpleWords: Place value is about where digits sit!

subject: Mathematics
title: Ravi and Priya's Marble Exchange
hook: What happens when two piles of marbles overflow one bag?

slides.title: The Big Trade
slides.storyContext: Ravi has 17 marbles. Priya has 15 marbles. They want to put all marbles into one bag. 'Will they fit together?' asks Ravi.
slides.inSimpleWords: When both numbers are big, carrying helps.

image.alt: The Big Trade — Addition with Carrying

slides.title: Line Up the Numbers
slides.storyContext: Priya draws two columns. 'Ravi, put ones under ones and tens under tens!'

points.label: Setup
points.text: 17 written as 1 ten and 7 ones. 15 written as 1 ten and 5 ones.

slides.inSimpleWords: Write tens above tens, ones above ones.

image.alt: Line Up the Numbers — Addition with Carrying

slides.title: Add the Ones First
slides.storyContext: Ravi adds the ones column: 7 + 5. 'That's 12 marbles!' But the ones bag only holds 9!
slides.inSimpleWords: 7 + 5 = 12, which is more than 9.

image.alt: Add the Ones First — Addition with Carrying

slides.title: Carry the Extra Ten
slides.storyContext: Priya says, 'Those extra 10 marbles make a new ten! Put 2 marbles here and carry the 1 ten up to the tens column.'

points.label: Carrying
points.text: Write 2 in ones place. Carry 1 ten to the tens column.

slides.inSimpleWords: When ones make 10 or more, carry a ten!

image.alt: Carry the Extra Ten — Addition with Carrying

slides.title: Add the Tens
slides.storyContext: Now Ravi adds the tens: 1 ten (from 17) + 1 ten (from 15) + 1 ten (carried) = 3 tens!

example.problem: Add 1 + 1 + 1 in the tens column (after carrying).

slides.inSimpleWords: The carried ten joins the tens column.

image.alt: Add the Tens — Addition with Carrying

slides.title: The Answer
slides.storyContext: Priya writes down: 3 tens and 2 ones = 32. 'Ravi, you have 32 marbles total!'
slides.inSimpleWords: 17 + 15 = 32 marbles in one big bag!

slides.title: Another Example: 24 + 18
slides.storyContext: Ravi wants to try again. Priya helps: 4 + 8 = 12. Carry the 1. Then 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. Answer: 42!
slides.inSimpleWords: 24 + 18 = 42. Carrying works every time!

slides.title: Carrying Makes Big Numbers
slides.storyContext: Priya says, 'When the ones add up to 10 or more, they become a new ten in the tens place. That's why it's called carrying!'

points.label: Why carrying?
points.text: Ones that make 10 or more become tens.

slides.inSimpleWords: Carrying moves extra ones to the tens place.

image.alt: Carrying Makes Big Numbers — Addition with Carrying

slides.title: Try This: 28 + 14
slides.storyContext: Ravi writes 28 + 14. 'The ones are 8 + 4 = 12. So I carry 1 and write 2. Then 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. Answer: 42!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Practicing carrying makes it easy!

slides.title: Word Problem
slides.storyContext: A shop has 26 red pens and 17 blue pens. Priya asks, 'How many pens in total?' Ravi calculates: 26 + 17 = 43 pens!

example.problem: There are 26 red pens and 17 blue pens. How many pens in total?

slides.inSimpleWords: Real problems use carrying all the time!

slides.title: Marble Lesson Ends
slides.storyContext: Ravi counts all 32 marbles into the big bag. 'Carrying is like upgrading! Small ones become tens!'

points.label: Review
points.text: 1. Write tens under tens, ones under ones. 2. Add ones first. 3. If ones make 10+, carry 1 ten. 4. Add tens (with the carry). 5. The answer is tens + ones.

slides.inSimpleWords: Carrying turns extra ones into new tens!

image.alt: Marble Lesson Ends — Addition with Carrying
